title: What brought down the Classic Maya cities
summary: Over 80 theories have been proposed and there is no universally accepted collapse theory, though drought has become the leading explanation in recent research.
why: A literate, crowded civilisation emptied its great cities, a case study for societies under stress.
question: Why were the southern Maya lowland cities abandoned in the Late Classic period?
evidence: Decline of the southern lowland city-states spans the 7th to 9th centuries CE.
wouldSettle: High-resolution, city-by-city records of drought, population and warfare dated to the decades of abandonment.

theories.name: Drought
theories.idea: Prolonged dry spells undermined farming and water supplies.

theories.name: Ecological overreach
theories.idea: Deforestation and soil erosion exhausted the land.

theories.name: Warfare and invasion
theories.idea: Conflict and outside groups disrupted the cities.

theories.name: Trade and authority breakdown
theories.idea: Loss of trade networks and of faith in kings unravelled society.
